Timeline::add_nanos¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::add_nanos(std::int64_t nanos) const

What It Does¶

Shifts every defined timestamp by a fixed nanosecond offset.

This is the low-level scalar-offset surface to use when your shift is already expressed in raw nanoseconds.

Parameters¶

nanos

The number of nanoseconds to add.

  • positive values move forward in time

  • negative values move backward in time

Returns¶

Timeline A shifted timeline.

Examples¶

Example 1. Add one second to every timestamp.

auto out = base.add_nanos(1'000'000'000LL);
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(out) << "\n";

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[4], tz=UTC)
[ 2024-11-01 09:00:01, 2024-11-01 10:15:31, 2025-01-01 00:00:00, 2025-01-01 00:00:01 ]

Notes¶

  • Absent instants remain absent.

  • Use add_duration(...) when the shift is already represented as a Duration.
